relevance_note: Single-patient case report of a man with a de novo NOD2 variant: "Subsequent gene screening revealed a de novo NOD2 mutation (c.1001G>A, chr16:50744823 p. Arg334Gln)".
method_note: Read by hand; JSON assembled with a short Python script in the scratch directory, spans checked verbatim by script. In scope: the patient plus his parents and sister, who were tested and found negative ('absent in his parents and sister'); the relatives have no variant rows and no reported phenotype, so their checklist items are all 'not reported'. CONTRADICTION: the case report and Figure 2 legend give the variant as c.1001G>A p. Arg334Gln, while the Abstract and Discussion call the same mutation p.R334W; the variant row records the cDNA with p. Arg334Gln (printed beside it); p.R334W appears only in the pathogenicity and functional spans. The functional statement is cited from ref 5 (literature), not an assay done on this patient's variant, and is attached to the p.R334W wording. No genome build is printed for chr16:50744823. Variant type not stated (left 'not reported'). Age: '22-year-old' is the age at presentation, recorded as age at last evaluation (time of report); follow-up continued 6 months after that; no age at onset is printed (only a '15-year history'), and no age at diagnosis is stated, so none was computed. Camptodactyly checklist item marked observed from the Figure 1 legend 'Symmetric flexion contractures of bilateral proximal interphalangeal joints 2 to 5' (the paper does not use the word camptodactyly). Bilateral retinal vasculitis (Figure 1d legend) is recorded as a feature but not as the checklist vasculitis item, whose definition lists large-vessel arteritis, aortitis or leukocytoclastic vasculitis. 'Intraocular pressure was normal' excludes raised intraocular pressure as a feature, but the composite checklist item 'glaucoma or raised intraocular pressure' is left not reported (narrow absence does not exclude glaucoma). 'no associated skin changes' used to exclude the skin rash checklist item. Table 1 (follow-up labs, e.g. hemoglobin 110 g/l below the 130-175 range) not turned into features because the paper does not name an abnormality for those values. The paper writes 'elevated serum creatine' in the case report and 'Serum creatinine' elsewhere; recorded as elevated serum creatinine. Ethnicity/country of origin not stated (only a Chinese funding and hospital context), left not reported.
